latest_rss.title: Global Terrorism Threat Looks Uncomfortably Familiar
latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula’s (AQAP) May 2026 Inspire propaganda releases coincided with the new U.S. Counterterrorism Strategy’s identification of al-Qaeda—particularly AQAP—as a primary external threat. 



Several indicators that preceded earlier external attack cycles are again visible today across al-Qaeda and Islamic State (IS) networks: namely, explicit calls for Western attacks, permissive sanctuaries, cross-theater facilitation, leadership guidance, rising arrests, and disrupted plots. 



The current threat environment is not a replica of the pre-9/11 period; it is more dispersed, technologically enabled, and networked. The danger lies in dismissing fragmented warning signs when fragmentation is now central to how the threat is evolving.

These revelations support Israeli airstrike justifications, but Hamas and PIJ seem to place a higher priority on publicly honoring their fallen militants. Both groups do not want to appear to abandon militants who are part of their combined media, political, and military ecosystems.
